newsitem.title: SWEDEN: H&M not optimistic about consumer situation.
newsitem.headline: H&M not optimistic about consumer situation.

text.p: Swedish clothing retailer Hennes & Mauritz said on Wednesday it was not optimistic about the consumer situation in Sweden.
"We are not especially optimistic. That is the general feeling," Jan Jacobsen, head of H&M's finance department, told Reuters.

A recent economic survey by pollster SKOP showed there were no signs that private consumption would turn upwards in the autumn. H&M is less exposed to volatility in consumption than other retailers with higher-priced goods, however.
"We are less sensitive to volatility but, of course, helped when consumption is high," Jacobsen said.
According to SKOP, 32 percent of Swedish households believed their living standards would fall in the coming year while only 14 percent believed it would be better.
At 1050 GMT the H&M share traded at 694 crowns, four above Tuesday's close.
